races.name: Sky Bet Mile Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Exclusive Code
runners_data.note: Won twice over this course and trip on good ground, James Doyle a strong booking for Archie Watson whose yard is quiet at present (0/25 in 14 days); prominent in style but has no soft-ground win on record and a pace-collapse scenario leaves her exposed late.

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has won four times, three over this exact 8f trip, and arrives fresh at 41 days off; prominent style suits a true-run race but soft-ground form is thin (1 placing from 8 soft-ground runs) and a contested early pace will test his stamina reserves.

runners_data.name: Outback Heat
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the most likely pace-setter; has won over C&D and carries strong form (1312), but faces a battle to dominate with Blue Courvoisier and Lion of Alba also wanting the lead — a contested gallop at his own end risks leaving him empty in the closing stages on this ground.

runners_data.name: Command The Stars
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose soft-ground record is better than his overall figures suggest (2 wins, 2 placings from 10 runs in similar conditions); Darragh Keenan takes over and the horse drops back to a more suitable 8f after a 11f run — stamina here is not an issue and the race shape suits his profile directly.

runners_data.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners_data.note: Has pace to burn and wants to lead; Clive Cox yard in good form (6/22 in 14 days) and Rossa Ryan is an astute front-running partner, but in a field this loaded with early speed Blue Courvoisier may find himself in a drag-race that suits nobody in front of her — winning from the lead is possible only if rivals check or hesitate at the break.

runners_data.name: Noelan Star
runners_data.note: Won twice at 8f on fast ground and has course and distance form; Daniel Tudhope keeps the ride for Edward Bethell whose yard is firing (9/25 in 14 days), and a prominent-style horse who can settle just off a fast pace is well placed tactically — soft ground is untested but breeding suggests it should not inconvenience.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out the highest-profile yard runner with Tom Marquand aboard; won at 8f on standard ground and finished second last time, but headgear (hood) is noted and a record of 9th and 10th in the last two runs before that second suggests inconsistency — needs the pace to be truly honest to grind out a finish.

runners_data.name: Lion of Alba
runners_data.note: A third confirmed front-runner whose record of four starts producing one win and three finishes of 4th or worse betrays the limits of his ability; headgear (tongue-tie) is in use, but Hugo Palmer's yard is subdued (1/28 in 14 days) and a horse who has finished 7th, 7th, 4th, 7th, 1st in career runs looks unreliable when the pressure is applied.

runners_data.name: Welbury
runners_data.note: The most compelling hold-up profile in the field — two wins and two seconds from five 8f runs, all on good ground, with the trainer Bethell doubly represented and in hot form; Oisin Orr gets the call, has run only 13 days ago which keeps him sharp, and a truly-run soft race is precisely the shape that flatters this horse's strong finishing pattern.

runners_data.name: Intense Vision
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won twice earlier this season but has posted three consecutive disappointing runs (11th, 20th, 3rd), with a specific fitness flag that this horse fades in the finish — hold-up style in a race where stamina is tested to the limit makes that fade tendency a serious concern, and the stable has only 2 runners in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Jeddaal
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground at 8f (1st from 1 soft run) and also on good ground at 7f and 8f, giving Kieran Shoemark a horse with genuine versatility of conditions; Ed Walker's yard is reasonably active (4/42) and a prominent style that can sit fourth or fifth in a strong-pace race suits — the drop back from a recent 4th is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Stepping up to a mile for the first time from a base of 6f and 7f wins — that is the central question for Marco Ghiani and Stuart Williams; won over 7f in good form and has placed from 5 runs, but a first try at 8f in a heritage handicap on soft ground with a pack of natural pace horses in front is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Bearish
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on a lightly-raced Ed Dunlop horse that has won twice and placed once from four starts — the combination of top jockey, shrewd trainer, and a prominent style that can be ridden to travel into the race rather than grind through it makes this one of the more interesting profiles; 47 days off may see him need the run but Murphy will ensure he gets a clear view from 2f out.

runners_data.name: Eklleem
runners_data.note: William Buick's mount from William Haggas's string has won over 8f on good ground but has only one run on soft (6th over 7f) and is a confirmed leader/pace-setter type who will be embroiled in the front-end battle; 64 days off is a long break and first-time soft at this trip with traffic ahead is a risk.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Colin Keane heads over from Ireland for G M Lyons with a horse that has placed eight times and posted a win on standard going — soft ground is untested but has run on it at 7f; headgear (tongue-tie and hood) noted, prominent style should see him competitive for a place even if his finishing kick is limited.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's horse won over 7f and finished second at 8f, giving the trip credentials, but with five or more natural front-runners ahead of him in this field, Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) will find Astrazar pushed wider and deeper than his natural prominent position — he is a true prominent racer operating from a disadvantaged midfield slot in this shape.

runners_data.name: Storming Point
runners_data.note: Has placed four times in five starts and shows consistency on both good and soft surfaces (2nd on soft over 8f and 10f), but in this field Rob Hornby will not find the prominent ground he needs — Storming Point is a natural stalker who will be bumped back into midfield by sheer weight of rivals, meaning his best form may be inaccessible here.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up runner has a habit of finding the frame without winning (2nd on soft last time) and James Sullivan knows the horse well; soft ground record is better than most (3 placings from 14 soft runs), but a tendency to finish 8th or worse in races without an honest pace is a concern — needs the leaders to truly collapse for his late run to materialise.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 6f and good over 7f, so conditions and trip are within range; Saffie Osborne takes over for Richard Spencer and headgear (tongue-tie and hood) is applied — hold-up style in a flat race at York with genuine pace is the ideal scenario but the horse's OR of 84 at the bottom of the weights means it needs everything to go perfectly.

runners_data.name: Le Samourai
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's runner is a confirmed front

races.paceDynamic: Outback Heat, Blue Courvoisier, Lion of Alba, and Le Samourai all want to lead, with Eklleem also capable of pressing from the front, meaning this 1m Good-to-Soft contest at York will be run at a relentless gallop from the off — there will be no tactical dawdle in a 20-runner handicap with this much early pace. The front end will be fully congested throughout the first half-mile, and the sustained pressure on soft ground will turn this into a genuine stamina test, with leaders likely to stop quickly in the closing stages as the ground saps their reserves. Midfield and hold-up runners will face traffic dangers between the 3f and 2f markers as the field fans out around the wide York turn, making position and clear runs at the 2f pole critical. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all realistically get their position — Storming Point and Astrazar are genuine prominent racers who will be shuffled into midfield by the sheer weight of speed ahead of them, with Outback Heat and Blue Courvoisier the most likely to actually dominate the early fractions. This race shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up and genuine late-finishing profiles — horses who settle behind the pace, conserve energy on the ground, and produce sustained finishes from 2f out will be at a significant advantage over anything that tries to make the running or sit close early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple front-runners burn each other off through an unsustainably fast early gallop on soft ground, setting it up for those held up off the pace.
scenarios.body: The leaders Outback Heat, Blue Courvoisier, and Lion of Alba will have expended significant energy fighting for position, and by the 2f pole the field will be strung out with the front rank stopping rapidly; hold-up horses travelling smoothly in mid-to-rear will sprint past the weakening leaders with fresh legs. Soft ground amplifies the collapse at the front, rewarding Welbury and Command The Stars who possess the stamina and finishing kick to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong but controlled gallop is set by one front-runner who gets a clear lead, stretching the field and setting it up for a staying-prominent type to stay on powerfully.
scenarios.body: One of Outback Heat or Blue Courvoisier breaks cleanly and gets a length's advantage, thereby avoiding the worst of the positional scrimmaging, and gallops at a stiff but metronomic pace that rewards horses with superior stamina and ability to travel just off a genuine pace. Prominent horses with proven soft-ground stamina — Noelan Star and Jeddaal — find themselves ideally placed three or four off the pace and can sustain their effort all the way to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Chaos Claims
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group of 8-plus runners creates severe interference between the 3f and 2f markers, forcing horses wide or checking their momentum at a crucial stage.
scenarios.body: The sheer congestion of Exclusive Code, St Anton, Zennor Storm, Ironwill, Bearish, Krasimir, and others all vying for the same mid-prominent berths will create a wall of horses across the York straight, and any runner caught flat-footed or forced wide will lose valuable lengths at the worst moment. The horses that benefit are those drawn wider who can bypass the scrimmage or those with the acceleration to thread through gaps — Bearish with Oisin Murphy's positional intelligence and Welbury from a clear early line stand out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Defies Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders, most likely Outback Heat, escapes uncontested at the front by outbreaking rivals and dictates a controlled, measured gallop rather than the frantic pace anticipated.
scenarios.body: In a 20-runner field it is conceivable that one leader breaks sharply and the others check or hesitate, allowing a single front-runner to control fractions and get an easy lead on ground that, while soft, does not fully negate a front-runner's advantage if the pace is honestly but not brutally fast. Outback Heat, who has already won over this course and distance, would be the primary beneficiary, with Le Samourai capable of tracking into a place.

races.name: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: Proven at 2m+ trips and handles soft ground well (4 similar-going runs, 3 places); Oisin Murphy gives him a significant tactical edge in navigating the prominent traffic scramble, and he must avoid the early congestion to land a blow from his natural front-rank position.

runners_data.name: Al Nayyir
runners_data.note: William Buick partners an 8-year-old who knows his job; soft ground is not a concern and his best form (wins at 14f and 16f on good-ish surfaces) suggests the extreme trip stretches him, though his hold-up style means he avoids the early positional battle entirely.

runners_data.name: Amiloc
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner and likely to dictate on a flat, galloping track; his recent form has been modest (three 6s and a U) and soft ground is unexplored territory based on his history, so his ability to sustain the lead into the straight is the key question of the race.

runners_data.name: Carmers
runners_data.note: Ran well to win at 16f on Good to Soft for trainer P Twomey earlier this season and gets on TV headgear; he will contest the prominent positions early but has to overcome the crowded berth and a lack of a prep run to show his best at this extreme trip.

runners_data.name: Columbus
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' lightly-raced stayer won over 17f earlier in career and has placed consistently at 20f; Colin Keane will ride him cold from his natural hold-up position, and the soft ground and extreme trip are both in his favour — the 20-day turnaround for a Mullins horse on soft ground is worth respecting.

runners_data.name: French Master
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 5-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose instinct will be to bowl along close to the pace, but with the prominent slots oversubscribed he is likely to end up racing in a position that doesn't suit him; James Doyle will try to make the best of it, though his chances are tempered by racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners an A P O'Brien runner who wants to be on the premises, having won over 22f last time and placed consistently — but the prominent group is too deep for all of them to get their slot, and Illinois may find himself further back than ideal; Moore's ability to place a horse is the only real mitigation here.

runners_data.name: Mount Atlas
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 5-year-old arrives in fine nick having won over 14f and placed twice recently on soft-ish ground; P J McDonald is adept at getting horses into position on a big track and Mount Atlas's consistent placed form (1-2-2-3) makes him a solid profile horse for this shape.

runners_data.name: Quickthorn
runners_data.note: The 9-year-old veteran has not run for 707 days — an extraordinary layoff — and while he has three career wins on soft ground and won over 14f on soft, the stable only has a 1/6 14-day record and the fitness question is enormous; his prominent style means he would naturally compete for a crowded berth if fit, but the layoff must dominate any assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Amiloc is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field over 2m½f on Good to Soft ground, he is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset — Rossa Ryan will have no reason to be pushed along and can settle into a rhythm that suits a galloping track like York. The prominent contingent is congested: Caballo De Mar, Carmers, Mount Atlas, French Master, and Illinois all want to race in the first three or four, meaning scrimmaging for position in the early stages is near-certain, with genuine traffic dangers developing between the two-furlong and three-furlong poles as the field compresses on the turn. French Master and Illinois are natural prominent horses redistributed to a midfield mapping because the race simply does not have room for all of them at the front — of the genuine prominent runners, Caballo De Mar (proven at the trip, Oisin Murphy) and Mount Atlas (strong recent form, P J McDonald) are best-placed to actually secure those slots. A controlled single-pace gallop on soft ground over this extreme trip favours horses who can travel sweetly in mid-division and produce a sustained, grinding finish — the hold-up profile of Al Nayyir and Columbus is particularly interesting, as is any prominent runner who avoids the early traffic scramble and emerges into clear daylight at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amiloc Controls, Grinders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Amiloc leads at a measured tempo and the prominent pack fails to dislodge him early, setting up a test of sustained stamina.
scenarios.body: Amiloc's honest gallop on soft ground creates a true staying test where the winner comes from just off the pace, grinding past in the final two furlongs; horses who travel smoothly in a prominent or mid-division position without burning energy in the early scrimmage are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage burns enough energy that the pace collapses in the straight, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Columbus and Al Nayyir, both gifted at coming from off the pace with patient jockeys in Colin Keane and William Buick, benefit most if the field strings out and gaps open on the turn; the extreme distance and soft ground amplify the stamina advantage of horses who conserve energy deepest in the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Caught
scenarios.trigger: If the early positional battle among the prominent group forces a faster-than-expected early pace, draining Amiloc and the front-runners before the straight.
scenarios.body: With multiple runners seeking prominent ground and Amiloc unable to dictate entirely unchallenged, the pace lifts enough to leave the front-runners vulnerable to late challenges from hold-up types who track the leaders without over-committing; this scenario most hurts Amiloc and Carmers but opens the race up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Midfield Winner
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems at the two-to-three furlong mark severely hamper the prominent group and neither the front-runner nor the closers finish clearly, allowing a midfield tracker to thread through.
scenarios.body: French Master or Illinois, despite being mapped out of their natural prominent role, could benefit if gaps appear at the right moment and their jockeys (James Doyle, Ryan Moore) are able to exploit a chaotic straight; this scenario is genuinely unlikely given both are racing out of their ideal position and depend on a messy outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch the scrimmage for prominent positions in the first half-mile: Caballo De Mar, Carmers, Mount Atlas, French Master, and Illinois all want to race close to Amiloc, and any runner caught in traffic or forced wide between the 3f and 2f marks could see their race effectively ended.

Amiloc's rider Rossa Ryan needs to judge the pace carefully — if the prominent pack pressures him into going faster than ideal on soft ground over this extreme trip, he could fold tamely in the straight and unbalance the whole race shape.

Quickthorn's 707-day absence is the single biggest fitness unknown in the field; if he returns below peak condition his prominent style could see him burn out early and interfere with the runners behind him in the final stages.

Columbus's 20-day turnaround under Willie Mullins on soft ground is worth monitoring in the betting market — Mullins targets these trips shrewdly and Colin Keane riding from the hold-up position means he will not be caught in the early prominent scramble.

Al Nayyir at age 8 brings experience but his best form has come at 14-16f rather than this extreme 2m½f; watch whether William Buick commits to a waiting ride or positions him closer than expected if the tempo looks genuinely slow.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's stable in good form (1/28 T14) and Oisin Murphy retains the ride; all six career starts show a front-running profile and Good to Soft is within range of his Good-ground wins, though he has yet to lead a field this competitive — the key risk is being dragged into an unwinnable speed duel by Hell Of A Spin and Final Objective.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has placed this horse well across five runs and Kieran Shoemark knows the track; his one soft-ground run at 6f produced a placing (2nd) which is directly relevant today, though patchy form otherwise (6-1-8-3-2) suggests consistency questions at this level.

runners_data.name: Arapaho Gold
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three runs for Michael Dods (3/27 T14) and Connor Beasley, with all victories on Good or better — Good to Soft is softer than anything he has faced, so the ground is the primary unknown; if he handles it, his racing style (prominent) and improving profile make him one of the most interesting participants.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago (a win at 6f on Good) which is an unusually short turnaround for a 2-year-old in a Group 2; James Doyle is high-class but the horse's front-running tendencies could lead to a costly early battle, and his trainer's T14 record is thin (1/3), making this a speculative step up in class.

runners_data.name: Great Oak
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's sole runner from this horse's one career run — a win at 6f on Good — carries the joint-highest OR (120) in the race, but the single-run profile means tactics and temperament in a 12-runner Group 2 on soft ground are unknowns; Clifford Lee will need a clear run from wherever the horse settles.

runners_data.name: Hell Of A Spin
runners_data.note: Steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time (all three runs over the shorter trip), which is a significant query for Adrian Keatley's front-runner on testing ground; M.P. Sheehy rides and the horse has the pace to lead, but whether it stays the extra furlong in these conditions is the central doubt.

runners_data.name: Marco Polo
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and A.P. O'Brien are the strongest trainer-jockey combination in the race, and the horse's one placing (2nd at 6f on Good) shows ability; his natural style is uncertain and he is mapped towards the rear because the field is short of genuine hold-up types — his actual race position will likely be more forward than the map implies, ridden to Moore's judgement.

runners_data.name: Matteo
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's two-year-old has won both starts (5f, Good) but has not run for 83 days, raising fitness questions for this sharp test; Kevin Stott rides and the horse's front-running style looks compromised by the depth of pace opposition, suggesting he may be asked to drop back and race off the pace rather than his preferred lead.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.note: George Scott's gelding was placed on his first two runs at 6f (2nd and 1st) before finishing 8th last time, and the 66-day absence adds a question mark; Tom Marquand is an able partner and the prominent style suits the track, though the reversal in form needs explaining before he can be trusted at Group 2 level.

runners_data.name: Mussab
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's lightly-raced (two runs, both thirds) colt has Colin Keane booked and has shown nothing wrong, merely undistinguished placings on Good; 62 days off and an unknown tactical role (OR=97 here suggests he needs to improve significantly) means this looks like an educational run rather than a winning mission.

runners_data.name: Never Enough
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant booking for Ed Walker's horse, who won over 6f on Good last time (LR: 27d); the lowest OR of the front-running group (86) means he is outclassed by several rivals on ratings, and Buick may choose to drop him in behind rather than fight for the lead — which would leave him in unfamiliar territory tactically.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: The only confirmed hold-up runner in the race for Nigel Tinkler (Silvestre De Sousa), with a progressive profile across 5f (1st, 2nd, then a drop to 4th) and now stepping to 6f for the first time; the extra furlong on soft ground theoretically helps a closer, but he is stepping both in class and distance simultaneously which compounds the ask.

races.paceDynamic: Five horses carry genuine front-running inclinations into this 6f Gimcrack — Adaay of Scarlett, Hell Of A Spin, Final Objective, Matteo, and Never Enough — guaranteeing a fierce early duel on ground that is Good to Soft, which will compound the attrition from a contested pace. Adaay of Scarlett has been prominent in all six starts and Hugo Palmer's stable is firing (1/28 over 14 days), while Hell Of A Spin (Adrian Keatley, steps up from 5f) and Final Objective (ran just seven days ago and may be ridden conservatively) add to the pressure from the front. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their desired positions; Matteo (83 days off, unknown sharpness) and Never Enough (lowest OR in that group) are most likely to be squeezed off the pace and forced to race wide or behind their preferred slot. With soft-ish ground bleeding speed out of the leaders from the two-furlong pole, this race shape strongly favours horses who race prominently but with enough tactical restraint to capitalise late — the Prominent-to-Midfield profile that can be delivered off the pace without being a genuine hold-up type.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Grinds Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running cluster (Adaay of Scarlett, Hell Of A Spin, Final Objective) burn each other out through the first three furlongs on soft ground, setting a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The early pace battle on Good to Soft churns up the ground and ensures the leaders tie up inside the final furlong, with prominent hold-your-position types hitting the line strongest; Arapaho Gold (unbeaten in three, handled softer than today) and Agamemnon (placed on soft at 6f) are perfectly placed to pick up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Horse Comes Good
scenarios.trigger: If Great Oak or Marco Polo — both OR=120 — translate their exceptional ratings into a prominent but unhurried run that allows them to pick through a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Great Oak (K.R. Burke, one run, highest OR in the race) has the raw ability to win from a stalking position if Clifford Lee gets a clean passage, while Marco Polo (Ryan Moore, A.P. O'Brien) has elite connections to manage the tactical demands even if his natural style is uncertain from one run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the early leaders — most likely Adaay of Scarlett — breaks cleanly, secures an uncontested rail position and controls the fractions rather than being dragged into an all-out duel.
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy is capable of setting a measured tempo that blunts the opposition without burning the horse off early; Adaay of Scarlett's six career runs provide the experience and resilience to sustain the lead on this track, and the soft ground, while a concern for most leaders, could suit a horse that relaxes into the bridle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace dissolves dramatically in the final two furlongs and genuine hold-up runners benefit from a true staying test at sprint distance.
scenarios.body: Ronson (Silvestre De Sousa, progressing form with a win over 5f) is the only confirmed hold-up runner in the field, and Mussab has run green but shown stamina; however, with Marco Polo technically redistributed to the rear rather than being a true come-from-behind type, the scenario carries lower weight as the field lacks authentic closers.

watchPoints.text: Adaay of Scarlett, Hell Of A Spin, and Final Objective are on a collision course for the early lead — watch whether any trainer/jockey combination elects to back off and take a prominent rather than lead role, because whoever blinks first shapes the entire race.

Arapaho Gold's unbeaten record is built entirely on Good or better ground — if the going is appreciably soft underfoot (racecourse reports suggest Good to Soft, but with recent rainfall), his chance could be materially undermined before a hoof is placed on the turf.

Great Oak and Marco Polo share OR=120 but each has only one career run — watch the market move in the hour before post, as money for either of these lightly-raced horses from elite yards (K.R. Burke, A.P. O'Brien) would be a meaningful signal.

Matteo has not run for 83 days and faces a step up in class and ground — watch the paddock for signs of fitness and whether Kevin Ryan has him sharp enough to take his place in what will be a furiously-run race from the first stride.

Marco Polo is mapped to the rear but Ryan Moore rarely commits a horse to genuine hold-up tactics unless the horse demands it — watch his early positioning, as Moore breaking forward would confirm the horse is more tractable than his single run suggests and would upgrade his scenario probability.

races.name: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Kevin Ryan who has struggled for form this year with a string of double-figure finishes; three runs in similar going yielded one top-15 finish and no wins or places, making soft-ground claims thin, and 66 days off adds an unknown fitness dimension.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Jim Goldie who showed winning form on soft with a course-and-distance victory in his recent history; Paul Mulrennan rides and this horse holds a forward style that should allow him to actually secure a prominent berth in this field, giving him a structural advantage.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on this Crisford-trained six-year-old who has form figures of 1-3-1 on good ground but has tongue-tie on; a prominent runner with strong recent form including two wins, and Buick's positional intelligence makes him a key player if he can assert forward.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn have been in form (T14: 1/12) and this six-year-old has soft-ground place form, but his true style is prominent and with this many pace-pressing types in the field Jason Hart will likely find him racing mid-division rather than where he wants to be.

runners_data.name: Night Raider
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's five-year-old is the race's primary front-runner with consecutive wins including one on soft at this distance; James Doyle knows how to manage the fractions and if he gets an uncontested lead he is the horse to beat — he is the structural cornerstone of this entire pace map.

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: Consistent placer for David Loughnane with three top-three finishes in his last five including two on soft, but naturally inclined to press the pace and Tom Marquand may find him shuffled wider and further back than ideal in this field, which tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Redorange
runners_data.note: Clive Cox four-year-old with a solid recent run record including two wins; carries tongue-tie and P.J. McDonald rides — a genuine prominent type who should be positioned close enough to the pace to benefit if the front pair tire, though no soft-ground wins registered.

runners_data.name: Rumstar
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's six-year-old has a clean profile of wins and places at 5f on good ground and shapes as a prominent type who should occupy a genuine forward position; Rob Hornby is well suited to 5f sprint tactics and this horse deserves respect on pace map fit.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old has four runs on good ground with two wins but soft-going record of 4th; naturally pushes forward but the redistribution reflects a field too full of pace to accommodate him, meaning Rossa Ryan may have less room than usual to dictate his position.

runners_data.name: Bacio
runners_data.note: Wesley Ward's three-year-old arrives with a strong form line including four wins from six starts; only 63 days since last run, limited racing history at 5f on soft, but Juan Hernandez is experienced at riding Americans abroad and raw ability makes him a threat at any pace shape.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on the Aidan O'Brien three-year-old who has three consecutive wins including a Group-level performance; hold-up style is his natural mode and he is the classiest closer in the field — soft ground may blunt his finishing kick but Moore's patience makes him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Asfoora
runners_data.note: Henry Dwyer's eight-year-old Australian-trained sprinter carries both tongue-tie and blinkers; recent form shows a string of minor placings but not winning, and four runs on going similar to today produced one placing — age and current form trajectory are concerns in this class.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's six-year-old tracked by Daniel Tudhope, a hold-up type whose recent form string of 6-1-5-0-5-0 reads better than it looks at a glance given the class level; one soft-ground win in her history but has not fired consistently enough to hold a leading claim here.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's five-year-old has a soft-going record of one run and no wins or places on similar ground; although naturally a forward-running type, the congested pace map means Barry McHugh will likely find her further back than her style demands, limiting her chance.

runners_data.name: Rayevka
runners_data.note: Graffard's four-year-old has the strongest wet-ground profile in the race with three wins from seven starts on soft or heavy; Mickael Barzalona is a high-class rider and this horse's 2nd and 1st in recent outings including on soft make her a key player if conditions truly ride testing.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old has a form string of five finishes without a win in the last five and no wins on comparable going; though naturally prominent, Kieran Shoemark will find him absorbed into the midfield pack in this field, reducing his chance to utilise that style.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old is the second confirmed front-runner alongside Night Raider; Colin Keane will likely push for the early lead, but Fitzella has finished outside the top four in all five recent starts and appears to be setting pace for others rather than winning it herself.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's two-year-old is the youngest and lightest-weighted runner in the race at 114lbs and has shown rapid development with two wins from five starts; Silvestre De Sousa rides and the filly is a natural forwardly-placed type who will find herself behind the pace in this competitive field, though raw ability warrants watching.

races.paceDynamic: Night Raider and Fitzella are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner sprint, and with Night Raider a genuine Group-class pacesetter having won this trip on soft ground and Fitzella likely to push from her low draw, the early gallop will be honest to strong rather than a dawdle. The soft going at York will stretch the field quickly, compressing recovery time for hold-up horses and placing a premium on travelling well within a length or two of the pace. Runners like Jm Jungle, Starlust, Time For Sandals, Heavenly Heather and Pershaada are natural prominent types who cannot all slot in behind the leaders in a field this size and will inevitably find themselves racing further back than their handlers would choose — the horses most likely to actually secure a forward berth are American Affair, Cover Up, Rumstar, Redorange and Bacio, who have stronger claims on those slots by class or draw. This race shape — genuine pace, soft ground, 5f — heavily favours horses who can press the leaders in the first two furlongs without scrubbing along, giving prominent-to-midfield chasers with proven soft-ground efficiency a structural advantage over true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Night Raider and Fitzella fight for the lead through the first furlong, honest fractions on soft ground set up a race won by a horse tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn fuel combating each other and the soft ground, leaving the race to a prominent horse who has been able to travel comfortably in second or third gear before asserting; soft ground rewards those with a strong stride rather than those who need manufactured pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates, Soft Bounce
scenarios.trigger: If Night Raider controls the tempo without meaningful challenge and Fitzella drops away early, the leader preserves enough energy to hold on under soft conditions.
scenarios.body: Night Raider's two recent wins — including on soft — demonstrate he can front-run without over-extending himself, and if the pace is controlled rather than contested he becomes very hard to reel in over this trip on an energy-sapping surface; this is a front-runner's shape only if the challenge dissolves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Night Raider and Fitzella is genuinely fierce and both fade inside the final furlong, creating a clear late-running opportunity.
scenarios.body: Mission Central is the primary beneficiary here as the most talented genuine hold-up horse in the race, possessing high form figures and the class to pick up a scramble; Ain't Nobody and Azure Angel are secondary options who come from off the pace but lack the same ceiling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Weave, Redistributed Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the bulk of the redistributed prominent types manage to find better positions than mapped, crowding the pace group and creating a messy mid-race pattern that suits a horse finding daylight late.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies on Starlust, Jm Jungle or Time For Sandals forcing their way forward against the grain of the pace map and generating a stop-start gallop with gaps to exploit; it is the least likely shape because those horses are structurally out of role and the soft ground will not allow the acceleration needed to manufacture position.

watchPoints.text: Night Raider's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest swing factor — if Fitzella pushes him through an unsustainably fast opening two furlongs on soft ground, every front-to-midfield runner benefits; if she drops back early, Night Raider becomes very hard to catch.

Rayevka's soft-ground record (3W5P from 7 runs on give) is the best strike rate for conditions in this field and is easy to overlook in a market dominated by bigger names — Barzalona is capable of dropping her in and picking off tiring leaders.

Mission Central and Ryan Moore represent the class hold-up combination in the race, but the question is whether 5f on soft allows sufficient late acceleration — watch for Moore to judge the pace from further back than usual and whether the field strings out enough to give him a clear run.

Bacio is lightly raced with limited soft-ground exposure, but Ward horses trained for fast-ground American sprinting can occasionally excel fresh on soft — the risk is the unknown, and if the ground rides slower than Good to Soft the Ward team's form-line becomes harder to evaluate.

With five runners genuinely redistributed out of natural prominent positions, watch for crowding and scrimmaging between the 3f and 2f marks as horses try to improve their positions simultaneously — draw position and early footwork from jockeys will matter disproportionately in this race.

races.name: Assured Data Protection Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Plage De Havre
runners_data.note: Placed at 12f on Good ground multiple times for Balding, comfortable in the prominent position he'll seek here; 48 days off is not a concern for this yard, but the cluster of rivals for those early seats makes a clean run into the first bend critical.

runners_data.name: Wave Rider
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse with a soft-ground win on his record (1W4P in similar going) and recent form showing a rebound at 10f; steps up to 14f for the first time but pedigree and style suggest it will suit, and Murphy's ability to find cover in a congested early field is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good for Doyle and Al Jehani but has been consistently mid-table in his last four — the one win in five recent outings came at Goodwood in less competitive company; soft-ground form reads 0W1P across 14 runs, which is a meaningful flag.

runners_data.name: Master Vintner
runners_data.note: Beckett's four-year-old has finished first or second in four of his last five, mostly at 12f on Good-to-Standard, and wore blinkers last time; the step to 14f is an open question, but his consistency and proximity to the pace under Rossa Ryan make him a key player if the trip doesn't find him out.

runners_data.name: Ernst Blofeld
runners_data.note: Al Jehani's second string here, held up by Tudhope, who won over 12f on Standard ground last time — his only Good-to-Soft experience is thin (not flagged as a concern but untested); needs the pace to quicken and soften his rivals late, and a moderate tempo makes life hard.

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on a horse who has finished second or third in five of his seven runs at 12f — reliable but not a winner at this level yet; soft-ground experience is thin (one run, unplaced), and a step up to 14f with Moore's trademark late delivery could work if the pace is even mildly honest.

runners_data.name: Master Builder
runners_data.note: 100 days off for Menuisier is notable, but this horse won on return last time at 12f on Good and has placed at 14f on Soft before (7/14 runs on that combination); if fresh and fit, his mid-prominent style and soft-ground stamina make him quietly interesting.

runners_data.name: Sportingsilvermine
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins recently at 10f and 12f on Good for Ghiani and Owen, with solid each-way record overall; needs to step forward in grade here and the 14f trip is an extension — likely to compete for a prominent pitch, and his form cycle is live.

runners_data.name: Say What You See
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (two wins in last four at 10-12f) and a natural prominent racer; however, in this field he's likely to find himself shuffled into a midfield role he doesn't naturally operate from, which tempers confidence despite the ability being clear under Garritty.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: Grassick's four-year-old has won twice recently and is clearly on a roll, but this is a step into deeper waters at a big York handicap, and his instinct to race prominently will be tested by the sheer volume of forward-going rivals — Lee will need to manufacture a position from what's available.

runners_data.name: Explode
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner in the field, Buick takes over on the back of back-to-back wins at 12f on Good; the jump to 14f on Good to Soft is the query, but an uncontested lead with a sustainable pace is exactly the platform this horse has exploited twice already — OR=85 is well below his rivals but the tactical advantage is real.

runners_data.name: Zanndabad
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer on a seven-year-old whose recent form is poor (two 8ths), though he has stamina in abundance (wins at 20-22f) and soft ground suits; this 14f trip is sharply shorter than his winning distances, and Spencer will have to manufacture an unlikely late burst — needs plenty to go right.

runners_data.name: Shadow Dance
runners_data.note: 139 days off for Menzies is a significant concern, and the tongue-tie plus blinkers combination suggests the yard is trying things; a horse who has won prominently before but whose recent form is uniformly poor (0,7,7,6 in last four) and who won't naturally get to the front in this field — hard to make a compelling case.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Bramley's second string — ran 1st and 2nd at 16f on Good earlier in his career but has gone backwards since, recording a 10th and two 5ths; dropping back to 14f from staying trips and held up by Clifford Lee means he needs a strong pace that may simply not materialise.

runners_data.name: Primo Lara
runners_data.note: Two wins in last four and in-form for Chapple-Hyam with Colin Keane up, winning at 10f and 12f recently on Good; soft-ground record is modest (1W1P in 15) but the horse is clearly progressing — hold-up style means he needs the pace to be honest enough to make his finishing kick count.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Won over 7f-8f recently and steps dramatically up in trip to 14f here — a horse whose natural home is in shorter-distance handicaps, and his prominent instincts will leave him racing out of position in a field where those berths are already oversubscribed; De Sousa has a mountain to climb on paper.

runners_data.name: Cuff It
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with just three career runs, won over 10f on Soft for Spencer last time, and the form is interesting — but this is a steep ask in a 17-runner heritage handicap at York; Saffie Osborne takes the ride, and a horse who wants to be prominent will struggle to secure that position among older rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Explode (William Buick, OR=85) is the sole confirmed front-runner and will stride to the front from the off, likely setting a measured, sustainable gallop on Good To Soft ground over 1m4f — a trip that rewards relaxed, economical leaders rather than those who burn early. Behind him, a dense cluster of prominent-style horses — Plage De Havre, Wave Rider, French Duke, Master Vintner, Tycoon, Master Builder, and Sportingsilvermine — will contest the early positions two through five, creating a congested, pushy pursuit pack that may actually do Explode's job for him by policing each other rather than closing him down. The hold-up contingent of Ernst Blofeld, Zanndabad, Genealogy, and Primo Lara will be forced wide or deep in the field, and with a controlled gallop rather than a genuine test, those closers face a stiff ask to reel in a relaxed, well-positioned leader who has never been pressured. This race shape firmly favours horses who can sit just behind Explode in a prominent pitch and quicken from there — pure hold-up horses are disadvantaged unless the pace genuinely collapses late. The field also holds more naturally prominent types than the race can accommodate: of the redistributed runners, Say What You See, Truth Be Told, and Sportingsilvermine are the most likely to actually secure a prominent berth given their recent form trajectories, while Jimmy Speaking, Cuff It, Shadow Dance, and Truth Be Told will be shuffled back against their instincts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Explode Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Explode sets a calm, uncontested lead and the prominent pack behind him runs a steady tempo through the first mile.
scenarios.body: Explode controls fractions and the horses immediately tracking him — particularly those in the top five of the prominent cluster — arrive at the two-furlong marker with energy in reserve; on Good To Soft the premium is on relaxed travel and a one-run finish rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chase Hotpot Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the seven-strong prominent contingent pushes forward aggressively in the early stages, creating a genuine test that sets the race up for closers.
scenarios.body: The early scramble for positions two through five elevates the overall tempo, softening the prominent runners late; hold-up horses who travel kindly and produce a sustained finish into the Good To Soft ground then become the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Explode Stays On, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field's prominent congestion is never resolved and the pack continues to race competitively against each other all the way to the straight, leaving Explode untroubled.
scenarios.body: With no rival committed to closing down the leader, Explode's recent back-to-back wins at 12f on Good-ground suggest he can simply extend his lead from the home turn; Buick's patient ride style suits a horse who has learned to relax in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Late Flier
scenarios.trigger: If the volume of prominent types causes significant interference or traffic two-to-three out, gifting a clean late run to one of the deeper-held horses.
scenarios.body: A chaotic mid-race reshuffle can create gaps that a hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick exploits despite the moderate overall tempo; this is a low-probability shape because genuine closers in this field are few and the pace is unlikely to be truly strong enough to guarantee a late advantage.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion danger between furlongs 10 and 8 — with seven horses (Wave Rider, Plage De Havre, French Duke, Master Vintner, Tycoon, Sportingsilvermine, Master Builder) all seeking a prominent position behind Explode, watch for early bumping and checking as they jostle on the first bend at York.

Explode (Buick) is 6 days off his last run and steps up to 14f for the first time — if this trip finds him out he could capitulate quickly once headed, turning the race on its head for any horse positioned just behind.

Shadow Dance (Fraser) is 139 days absent with headgear changes and poor recent figures — a likely non-factor, but watch for erratic early running that could unsettle nearby rivals in the first few furlongs.

Truth Be Told and Say What You See are both on winning streaks but will be racing in roles that don't suit their natural style — if either manages to manufacture a genuinely prominent pitch early (particularly Truth Be Told from a good draw), upgrade their chance significantly over what the map suggests.

Zanndabad (Spencer) has stamina to burn at distances far beyond 14f — if Good to Soft deteriorates toward Soft-Heavy in the second half of the card, his low cruising speed becomes a bigger asset and his hold-up position more dangerous in the closing stages.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Naga
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR=95, trained by Gosden with Buick booked, but her five recent runs have all come on Good ground and she has zero wins or places in similar going — soft conditions are an untested variable; she wants to track prominently and should get a clean position just off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Sharpen
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in six soft-ground runs without winning, and her last two outings are a distant seventh and ninth in handicaps — form is in decline; Jamie Spencer will try to hold a prominent position but she arrives here 48 days off and her recent trajectory is worrying.|

runners_data.name: Janey Mackers
runners_data.note: Has two wins and three places from nine soft-ground runs, making her one of the most proven soft-going fillies in the field; Menuisier sends her 105 days fresh but she won at 1m on soft previously and the step back to a stamina trip here could see her hold-up style pay dividends late.|

runners_data.name: Lady Dora Mae
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Boughey and she has been consistently placed in 12 of 12 career runs with no fewer than two seconds in similar going — she is a model of consistency but her inability to win off this OR is a concern; she was run just seven days ago and should be fit to strike from a prominent berth.|

runners_data.name: Plaid
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Fanshawe filly who has won twice and placed twice at trips up to 9f — the step up to 1m2½f on soft ground is genuinely unexplored for her; she wants a prominent position and should get one, but stamina at this trip in this going is a legitimate question.|

runners_data.name: Electrifarhh
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old naturally wants to race prominently — hg:h headgear suggests she can be keen — but with seven rivals also targeting that berth she is almost certain to be squeezed back into midfield; her STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 confirms she will be racing against her grain, and her recent run of 3-6-7-2-1 at trips well short of today's is an additional concern.|

runners_data.name: Rastnet
runners_data.note: John Butler's filly has placed in four of her last five but exclusively on Standard artificial surfaces — she has just one run on turf in similar going and that form barely translates; she wears a hood and wants a prominent position which she should get in a mid-pack slot.|

runners_data.name: Patagonia Girl
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old is a hold-up type and her record shows a win over 12f on Good — the longest trip in this field suits her style; Ashley Lewis claims 3lb and the combination of a light weight and a patient ride could see her benefit if the pace is searching enough.|

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: Two wins from her last two starts, both on Good ground at 10f, make her an unexposed improver from William Haggas's yard; Saffie Osborne rides and her hold-up style is genuine — she has Topspeed figures (hg:t, meaning tongue tie) and her upward trajectory is the most compelling narrative in this race at her OR of 86.|

runners_data.name: Dream Camp
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding filly who won at 10f on Good and was placed at 7f on Standard — today's 1m2½f on soft is a significant test of both trip and going; she sits in the prominent group and her profile suggests she is better suited to rattling good ground where she can travel freely.|

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston sends this three-year-old who has been in steady decline — 1-1-0-6-5-6 in her last six — and her sole soft-ground win came at 10f; she wants a prominent position but her current form does not inspire confidence in a 17-runner competitive handicap.|

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's confirmed front-runner has placed four times in six runs and won at 10f on Good — she will go forward and attempt to dictate; Edward Greatrex is a lesser-profile booking for a yard this active (T14:8/29) and at OR=84 her ability to sustain the lead against Pendella and Dunkeld Dreamer over soft ground is the central race question.|

runners_data.name: Callianassa
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old is naturally a prominent-racing type but her form in this field means she has been mapped to midfield — racing out of role with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 is a significant negative; recent form of 5-7-6-7-6 at shorter trips on Standard ground offers little encouragement for 1m2½f on soft turf.|

runners_data.name: Pendella
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old is a genuine front-runner who won last time at 10f on Good and placed on soft — she has the most credible soft-ground profile of the three pace-setters; Jack Nicholls claims 3lb and the light weight is relevant, but the dual front-runner duel with stablemate Dunkeld Dreamer risks them burning each other out.|

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: Stablemate to Pendella and another confirmed Burke front-runner, she won over 12f on Good and has placed on soft going — the trip is proven and the stable is firing (T14:8/32); Cam Hardie rides and the risk is that two K.R. Burke pace-setters effectively neutralise each other by fighting for the same position.|

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: Easterby's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up filly who has won twice on Good at up to 10f — soft going is a genuine question mark despite OR=78 giving her a handy pull at the weights; Fentiman rides and 42 days off could mean she arrives fresh enough to produce a big run if the closers' scenario materialises.|

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: A six-year-old veteran wearing a visor, trained by the small Kevin & Lauren Frost yard (T14:1/10), and her best form is at 11f on Standard ground — soft turf at York over this trip looks a stretch; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim helps but her recent string of 9-7-8-5-2 results on various surfaces gives little confidence at this level.|

races.paceDynamic: Food For Thought, Pendella, and Dunkeld Dreamer are all confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset, guaranteeing a strong, searching gallop over 1m2½f on Good to Soft ground at York — a combination that will ruthlessly expose any stamina limitations. Seven of the 17 runners are hunting prominent positions, creating a congested early-middle sector that will generate significant traffic risk two to three furlongs out, where the field funnels and those trapped wide or behind a wall of rivals will be vulnerable. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate, and of those, Food For Thought, Naga, Lady Dora Mae, and Plaid are best-placed to actually secure early positions, while Electrifarhh and Callianassa — genuine prominent horses by nature — will be shuffled back through no fault of their own. This pace scenario, with a genuine three-way fight for the lead on soft-ish ground over an extended trip, strongly favours genuine hold-up closers with proven stamina and soft-ground form, who can track wide of traffic and pick up the pieces from a race run at an honest, honest gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight it out early and the strong gallop stretches the field, setting up a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: Food For Thought, Pendella, and Dunkeld Dreamer burn each other up through a fast early tempo, and the soft-ish ground ensures those who chase hard from prominent positions also fade; genuine hold-up fillies with stamina and soft-ground credentials arrive late down the outside with momentum. This shape most rewards those who have been patient, have proven form in similar going, and whose jockeys can navigate the mid-race traffic to deliver a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three lead-competing front-runners gets a clear lead and the others blink or lose their footing in the early exchanges.
scenarios.body: Rather than a war of attrition between the pace-setters, one — most likely Food For Thought, who has the most consistent front-running profile — steals a march and settles into a controlled rhythm, conserving enough to hold on; the prominent types chasing from just off the pace are then the nearest threats as the field strings out. This rewards a horse who can dictate its own tempo and those sitting a length or two off the leader in the first two, rather than the deeper hold-up horses who have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace burns off the leaders at the two-furlong pole and a horse sitting third or fourth bounces off the pace to score.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners exhaust each other but not before they have pulled the field along at a clip that also drains the deep hold-up horses; the winner emerges from the prominent tracking position, having had cover without taking a lead, and quickens in the final furlong. Naga and Lady Dora Mae, both sitting just off the pace with top-tier jockeys in Buick and Moore, are best equipped to time a run from this position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Blocked, Race Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the traffic chaos two to three furlongs out catches the hold-up horses flat-footed and the pace collapses to a slow final half-mile.
scenarios.body: The congested mid-race group creates a concertina effect as the front-runners tire simultaneously, leaving hold-up horses with no gap to thread through and prominent horses ahead gifted a soft final furlong; this is the least likely shape but would benefit a prominent type who has sneaked a good draw and stayed out of trouble. Electrifarhh and Callianassa, though racing out of their natural role in this field, could theoretically benefit — though their STYLE_FIT tags and redistribution mean this scenario is structurally fragile.

watchPoints.text: Food For Thought, Pendella, and Dunkeld Dreamer will fight three-way for the early lead — watch for one being crowded out or checked before the first bend, which could cause a chain reaction through the prominent group behind them.

The seven prominent-seeking runners create a genuine traffic flashpoint two to three furlongs from home — horses like Janey Mackers and Silver Lake tracking from hold-up positions must be delivered wide and early or risk being swallowed by a wall of tiring rivals.

Pendella and Dunkeld Dreamer are K.R. Burke stablemates both confirmed as front-runners — watch whether they run in coordination or genuinely fight each other for the lead, as the latter outcome will almost certainly burn both out well before the line.

Electrifarhh and Callianassa, both natural prominent types forced into midfield by the volume of pace in this field, may attempt to push up early regardless — if they do, the field becomes even more congested and the closers gain further advantage.

Silver Lake's two recent wins both came on Good ground at 10f — watch her market move closely; if supported, punters have intelligence on how she handles today's softer conditions over a longer trip that the form book does not yet reveal.
